purpose: A domain may serve as the held-out evaluation domain exactly once. After an evaluation has read it, it has been seen: any later result on it is a result about a domain the system was tuned against, whether or not anyone intended that.
rules: A domain must be registered here, with a freeze date, BEFORE it is used as held-out.
An evaluation that names a held-out domain records itself in that domain's used_by list.
A domain with a non-empty used_by list may not be named as held-out again.
A domain whose role is 'development' can never become held-out, however long ago it was last read.
Removing or rewriting an entry to reuse a domain is a change to the pre-registration: it requires a new gate version and a written reason, not an edit here.

eat_t1dm.note: The main benchmark. Used continuously to build the system, so it can never serve as held-out.

melanoma.note: Frozen as a cross-domain checkpoint, then read repeatedly to diagnose and fix D6B-01..04 and the Phase 8 scope defect. Whatever it was at the freeze, it is now a development domain.

note: This list is empty on purpose. Nothing the project currently owns can serve as a held-out domain, which is the honest statement of where the cross-domain claim stands.
